Data_Files.title: Email from CEO of Urban Nutrients (Janice Wong)
Data_Files.content: Hi Team, We need to prepare for the 'Future Food HK' summit. I need Task 5 to focus on our new vertical farm open day for the public. For Task 6, write to the Environmental Bureau inquiring about the new energy subsidies for LED farming. Task 7 is a summary for our investors on why lab-grown meat is a safer bet for HK. For the senior team (B2), Task 8 is a formal proposal for the 'Northern Metropolis Food Security Zone'. Task 9 is an Op-Ed regarding the ethical backlash against synthetic beef, and Task 10 is the quarterly impact report. Please check the survey data and the recent article on the 'Brownfield Farm' project. Janice.

Data_Files.title: Newspaper Clipping: The Hong Kong Post
Data_Files.content: The controversy surrounding lab-grown meat grows as traditional farmers protest at the Legislative Council. Critics argue that 'cell-based' protein lacks the soul of traditional farming. However, data shows HK imports 98% of its beef. Dr. Simon Ng claims cultured meat uses 90% less land and 70% less water. Public concern remains high regarding the 'chemical' nature of the growth serum, despite FDA-style assurances from local labs.

Data_Files.title: Fact Sheet: Vertical Farming vs. Traditional Farming
Data_Files.content: Vertical Farming: 365-day harvest, zero pesticides, 95% water reduction, high initial capital (CAPEX), low transport emissions. Traditional: Weather dependent, high land use, high water waste, seasonal crops. Note: HK has over 1,000 hectares of abandoned farmland in the New Territories that could be converted to high-tech hubs.

Data_Files.title: Survey Results: HK Citizens' Attitudes toward Food Tech
Data_Files.content: 65% of respondents (n=1200) are willing to try lab-grown meat if priced under $60/lb. 80% prefer locally grown vertical farm vegetables over imports. 45% expressed concern over 'long-term health effects' of synthetic food. 90% believe food security is a 'critical' issue for HK's future.

Data_Files.title: Internal Memo: Logistics & Energy Costs
Data_Files.content: Recent electricity price hikes by HK Electric have increased our vertical farm operating costs by 12%. We must emphasize our 'Smart Grid' integration in the next proposal. Our Kwun Tong site has achieved a record harvest of 5,000 bags of kale per week. Demand from luxury hotel chains is up 40%.

Data_Files.title: Webpage: Northern Metropolis Agri-Development Plan
Data_Files.content: Vision: To create a 500-hectare food belt. Focus: High-density fish farming and hydroponics. Incentives: 5-year tax holiday for tech startups. Requirement: Must employ at least 20% local agricultural graduates.

Task_5.title: Public Open Day Information Leaflet
Task_5.instructions: Create a leaflet for the 'Urban Nutrients' Open Day. Include dates, location, highlights of vertical farming tech, and a section addressing 'Why Local?'

Task_6.title: Letter of Inquiry to the Environmental Bureau
Task_6.instructions: Write a formal letter inquiring about the 'Agri-Tech Energy Subsidy'. Mention current cost pressures and the environmental benefits of the Kwun Tong facility.

Task_7.title: Investor Email Summary
Task_7.instructions: Write a short email to potential investors summarizing the market potential for cultured meat in HK, citing the survey data and land use benefits.

Task_8.title: Proposal: Northern Metropolis Food Security Zone
Task_8.instructions: Write a formal proposal to the government. Detail the integration of vertical farming and lab-grown meat labs. Address land use, employment of local graduates, and food import reduction targets.

Task_9.title: Op-Ed: The Ethics and Reality of Future Food
Task_9.instructions: Write an opinion piece for the Hong Kong Post. Counter the arguments made by traditional farmers and address the public's health concerns using scientific data.

Task_10.title: Quarterly Impact Report
Task_10.instructions: Complete the report for the Board. Focus on the Kwun Tong site's output, the impact of electricity costs, and strategic recommendations for the upcoming year.

Script.Task_1_Script: Marcus: Good morning, I'm here to register for the booth. I'm Marcus Thornton from Green Horizon Agri-Tech. / Officer: Welcome, Marcus. Let me pull up your file. You're at booth B14-C, is that right? / Marcus: Correct. I'm the Senior Logistics Manager. You can reach me at thornton.m@greenhorizon.hk. / Officer: Great. Now, about your display. We have a note here about weight. / Marcus: Yes, the vertical rack is heavy, about 450 kilograms. We'll need a reinforced floor tile. And our LEDs are power-hungry—3000 Watts minimum. / Officer: Noted. Will you be giving away food? / Marcus: Yes, samples of our micro-greens and hydroponic lettuce. I have our FEHD health permit here, number FEHD-8821-X. / Officer: Perfect. Setup is November 14th, and you must teardown after 9:00 PM on the final day. Who is your insurer? / Marcus: Global Shield Underwriters. / Officer: Thank you. (120-second pause) This is the end of Task 1.
Script.Task_2_Script: Dr. Beatrice Lam: Welcome to SkyFarms. We are located right here in this old industrial block in Kwun Tong. By using 15,000 square meters of vertical space, we save immense land. Our system is closed-loop, meaning 98% water recycling. People ask why we are carbon neutral. Well, we don't just use green energy; we've installed a system that captures CO2 from the heavy traffic on the nearby highway and pumps it into the grow-rooms to boost plant growth. We get 22 crop cycles a year, far more than a traditional farm's 3 or 4. No pesticides—just UV-C light sterilization. We produce 1.2 tons of greens daily for Pure-Life Supermarkets. Our main cost? Electricity for the lights. Join our public tours every second Saturday. We are funded by the Agri-Tech Innovation Fund. (120-second pause) This is the end of Task 2.
Script.Task_3_Script: Host: Today we discuss lab-grown meat. Dr. Smith, your thoughts? / Dr. Smith: It's a miracle, but production scalability is the wall. We can make a burger, but can we make a million tons? / Sarah Chen: My focus is ethics. We remove the animal from the equation. No slaughter. It's the ultimate animal welfare win. / David Ho: True, but Sarah, it won't matter if it's expensive. We need price parity with traditional meat before HKers buy in. / Dr. Smith: Market share could hit 35% by 2040. We use synthetic amino acids as a growth medium now, no more fetal bovine serum. / Sarah Chen: And current prices in HK are $450 per kilo. Too high. / David Ho: We're working on 'aromatic fat scaffolding' to make it taste like real steak. / Sarah Chen: The government must require 'Cultivated' as a prefix on labels. / Dr. Smith: Come try it at the Science Park Bistro next week. (120-second pause) This is the end of Task 3.
Script.Task_4_Script: Host: Secretary, how secure is our food? / Secretary: Not very. We import 92% of everything. Our 2050 strategy targets 15% local production by 2040. We are prioritizing tubers and brassicas—filling foods. We'll zone new 'Multi-storey Agri-hubs' in the Northern Metropolis. We also have 'Edible Schools' to teach kids to grow food. We've added a 15-day buffer to our rice reserves. It's a $12 Billion plan. Our hurdle? Fresh water. But we're launching the Young Agri-Entrepreneur Loan to get youth involved. Consultations end January 20th. (120-second pause) This is the end of Part A.
